title: 1950 AHSME Problem 50
statement: A privateer discovers a merchantman \(10\) miles to leeward at \(11{:}45\) a.m. and with a good breeze bears down upon her at \(11\) mph, while the merchantman can only make \(8\) mph in her attempt to escape. After a two hour chase, the top sail of the privateer is carried away: she can now make only \(17\) miles while the merchantman makes \(15.\) The privateer will overtake the merchantman at:

solutions.text:
During the first two hours, the number of miles the privateer gains is \[ 2(11-8)=6, \] reducing the gap from \(10\) miles to \(4\) miles at \(1{:}45\) p.m.

After the damage, the ships’ speeds are in the ratio \(17:15.\) Since the merchantman still travels at \(8\) mph, the privateer’s new speed is \(8\cdot\tfrac{17}{15}=\tfrac{136}{15}\) mph. The closing speed is therefore \(\tfrac{136}{15}-8=\tfrac{16}{15}\) mph, so the number of hours needed to close the remaining gap is \[ \frac{4}{\frac{16}{15}}=\frac{15}{4}=3\frac34. \] Adding \(3\) hours \(45\) minutes to \(1{:}45\) p.m. gives \(5{:}30\) p.m.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Find the remaining gap after the first two hours
After the sail is lost, the speed ratio is \(17:15\) while the merchantman still travels at \(8\) mph
